subject: HEALTH
title: Driver Education (S1) & First Aid/CPR + Health II (S2)
description: Semester 1 is a classroom Driver Education course built on the California DMV Driver Handbook, covering the topics required before a minor may apply for an instruction permit at 15½: licensing and the provisional (GDL) rules, vehicle controls, signs and pavement markings, right-of-way, speed laws, lane use and parking, freeway driving, sharing the road, hazardous conditions, impaired and distracted driving, and collisions and insurance; it ends with full-length practice knowledge tests. Semester 2 combines First Aid, CPR and AED skills with Health II topics: mental and emotional health, substance use prevention (including fentanyl awareness), nutrition and consumer health, healthy relationships, and community and environmental health.
framework: California DMV Driver Handbook (current edition) and CA Education Code driver-education requirements; 2008 California Health Education Content Standards (Grades 9–12); 2019 CA Health Education Framework

standards.DE-1: Licensing: instruction permit requirements (age 15½, driver ed, knowledge and vision tests), provisional license rules (6-month permit, 50 supervised hours incl. 10 at night, passenger and 11 p.m.–5 a.m. restrictions), and license classes.
standards.DE-2: Vehicle readiness: controls, instruments, pre-drive checks, seat/mirror adjustment, seat belts, airbags, and child passenger restraints.
standards.DE-3: Traffic signs (shapes and colors), traffic signals, and pavement markings and lane lines; curb colors.
standards.DE-4: Right-of-way rules at intersections, roundabouts, crosswalks, and for pedestrians and emergency vehicles.
standards.DE-5: Turning, signaling, lane changes, passing, U-turns, lane positioning, and parking (including hills and parallel parking).
standards.DE-6: Speed laws: the Basic Speed Law, maximum and posted limits, school and residential zones, and following distance.
standards.DE-7: Sharing the road with pedestrians, bicyclists (3-foot rule), motorcyclists, large trucks, buses, light rail, and slow-moving vehicles.
standards.DE-8: Freeway driving: entering, merging, exiting, carpool/HOV lanes, and interchanges.
standards.DE-9: Hazardous conditions and defensive driving: night, rain, fog, wind, smoke, skids, space cushions, scanning, and the Move Over law.
standards.DE-10: Alcohol and drugs: effects on driving, BAC limits (0.08 adults; 0.01 under 21), implied consent, open-container and DUI penalties.
standards.DE-11: Distracted and drowsy driving: California cell-phone laws (minors may not use any wireless device), and fatigue management.
standards.DE-12: Collisions and emergencies: what to do after a collision, reporting (SR-1), insurance and financial responsibility, vehicle emergencies, and the point count system.
standards.DE-13: Railroad crossings, school buses, work zones, and special road situations.
standards.DE-14: Preparation for the DMV knowledge test: test-taking strategies and full practice examinations.
standards.H-HS.1.1.S: Describe ways to reduce the risk of injuries as a driver or passenger, including seat belt use and avoiding impaired driving.
standards.H-HS.1.4.S: Explain the relationship between substance use, distraction, and fatigue and the risk of motor-vehicle injuries.
standards.H-HS.1.9.S: Describe the procedures for basic first aid, CPR, choking, and use of an AED.
standards.H-HS.5.1.S: Use a decision-making process to evaluate risky situations, such as riding with an impaired or distracted driver.
standards.H-HS.7.2.S: Demonstrate basic first aid and CPR/AED procedures.
standards.H-HS.8.1.S: Encourage others to adopt safe behaviors, including safe driving practices.
standards.H-HS.1.2.M: Describe the signs, symptoms, and treatment of common mental health conditions, including depression and anxiety.
standards.H-HS.1.5.M: Identify warning signs of suicide and appropriate ways to seek help for self and others.
standards.H-HS.3.1.M: Identify trusted adults and community resources (including 988) for mental health support.
standards.H-HS.7.1.M: Practice stress management and coping strategies.
standards.H-HS.4.1.M: Use effective communication and conflict-resolution skills.
standards.H-HS.1.2.A: Explain the short- and long-term effects of alcohol, cannabis, nicotine/vaping, and other drugs, including fentanyl.
standards.H-HS.2.1.A: Analyze influences such as media, peers, and advertising on substance use.
standards.H-HS.4.2.A: Demonstrate refusal and negotiation skills to avoid substance use.
standards.H-HS.3.2.A: Locate valid information and services for substance use prevention and treatment, including naloxone access.
standards.H-HS.1.1.N: Explain the relationship between nutrition, physical activity, and health, and interpret food labels.
standards.H-HS.6.1.N: Develop a personal plan for healthy eating and physical activity.
standards.H-HS.2.1.P: Evaluate health products, services, and advertising claims as an informed consumer.
standards.H-HS.1.6.P: Explain how environmental factors such as air quality and water affect personal and community health.
standards.H-HS.1.3.G: Describe characteristics of healthy and unhealthy relationships, consent, and how to prevent dating violence.
standards.H-HS.1.6.G: Explain how to access reproductive and sexual health services and accurate information (CA Healthy Youth Act).

units.title: Licensing, the Vehicle and Driver Readiness
units.big_idea: Driving is a privilege earned step by step through California's graduated licensing system.

units.title: Signs, Signals, Markings and Right-of-Way
units.big_idea: Shared rules make traffic predictable and safe.

units.title: Navigating Roadways and Sharing the Road
units.big_idea: Safe drivers position, signal and communicate with every road user.

units.title: Hazards, Impairment and Distraction
units.big_idea: Most collisions are preventable when drivers manage risk, stay sober and stay focused.

units.title: Collisions, Insurance and Permit Test Prep
units.big_idea: Knowing the law and what to do in emergencies prepares you for the permit test and the road.

units.title: First Aid, CPR and AED
units.big_idea: Trained bystanders save lives in the first minutes of an emergency.

units.title: Mental and Emotional Health
units.big_idea: Mental health is health; skills and support help everyone cope.

units.title: Substance Use Prevention
units.big_idea: Accurate information and refusal skills protect health and futures.

units.title: Nutrition, Consumer and Environmental Health
units.big_idea: Informed choices about food, products and environment shape lifelong health.

units.title: Healthy Relationships and Final Assessment
units.big_idea: Respect, consent and communication are the foundation of healthy relationships.

objectives: Explain permit and provisional license requirements

days.title: Why GDL?
days.work: Read teen crash statistics and explain why California uses graduated licensing; write three questions you want answered this semester.

days.title: Permit requirements
days.work: Read the handbook licensing section and list every requirement to get a permit at 15½ (driver ed, application, vision and knowledge tests, parent signature).

days.title: Provisional rules
days.work: Create a one-page chart of provisional license restrictions: 11 p.m.–5 a.m. limit, no passengers under 20 without a 25+ licensed adult for 12 months, and exceptions.

days.title: Practice hours plan
days.work: With a parent, draft a 50-hour supervised driving log template including 10 night hours and behind-the-wheel training sessions.

days.title: Quiz
days.work: Take a 15-question handbook-style quiz on licensing rules.

objectives: Identify vehicle controls and gauges
Perform a pre-drive check

days.title: Controls tour
days.work: Sitting in a parked car with a parent, locate and explain every control: lights, wipers, hazards, defroster, parking brake and gear selector.

days.title: Dashboard
days.work: Use the owner's manual to identify 10 dashboard warning lights and what action each requires.

days.title: Pre-drive check
days.work: Do a walk-around check (tires, lights, fluids under the car, windows) and a cockpit check (seat, mirrors, belt) and time yourself.

days.title: Mirrors & blind spots
days.work: Adjust mirrors using the BGE method and have a family member walk around the car to map blind spots.

days.title: Check
days.work: Demonstrate the full pre-drive routine for a parent with a checklist.

objectives: Explain seat belt, airbag and child restraint laws
materials: egg, toy car and rubber band (crash demo)

days.title: Crash physics
days.work: Run an egg 'passenger' crash demo on a ramp with and without a rubber-band seat belt and explain inertia.

days.title: Belt & airbag laws
days.work: Read handbook rules on seat belts and child restraints (children under 2 rear-facing; under 8 in a car seat or booster in the back seat).

days.title: Airbag safety
days.work: Explain safe seating distance from airbags and why children ride in back.

days.title: Persuade
days.work: Create a 30-second PSA script encouraging peers to buckle up every ride.

days.title: Unit 1 test
days.work: Unit 1 test on licensing, controls and occupant protection.

objectives: Identify signs by shape, color and meaning

days.title: Shapes & colors
days.work: Make flashcards for sign shapes and colors (octagon stop, triangle yield, pentagon school, round railroad, pennant no passing).

days.title: Regulatory signs
days.work: Study regulatory signs and sort 20 sign images into must-do and must-not-do.

days.title: Warning & guide signs
days.work: Study warning and guide signs and explain each to a family member.

days.title: Sign hunt
days.work: On a ride as a passenger, photograph or list 15 different signs and explain what a driver must do at each.

days.title: Quiz
days.work: Sign identification quiz (40 signs, 90% goal).

objectives: Interpret signals, lane lines and curb colors

days.title: Signals
days.work: Study solid, flashing and arrow signals and what to do when a signal is out (treat as all-way stop).

days.title: Lane lines
days.work: Diagram yellow vs. white lines, broken vs. solid, double solid and two-way left-turn lanes.

days.title: Curb colors
days.work: Learn curb colors: red no stopping, yellow loading, white passenger loading, green limited time, blue disabled parking.

days.title: Street view
days.work: Use an online street-view map to identify markings at three local intersections.

days.title: Quiz
days.work: Quiz on signals and markings.

objectives: Apply right-of-way rules

days.title: Intersections
days.work: Use toy cars on paper intersections to model four-way stops, uncontrolled and T-intersections.

days.title: Roundabouts
days.work: Study roundabout rules (yield to traffic in the circle, travel counterclockwise) and diagram entering and exiting.

days.title: Pedestrians
days.work: Learn pedestrian right-of-way at marked and unmarked crosswalks and blind pedestrians with white canes or guide dogs.

days.title: Emergency vehicles & school buses
days.work: Learn to pull right and stop for emergency vehicles and to stop for flashing red school bus lights.

days.title: Scenario quiz
days.work: Solve 15 right-of-way scenarios and explain each answer.

objectives: Apply the Basic Speed Law
Use the 3-second rule

days.title: Basic Speed Law
days.work: Read and explain the Basic Speed Law: never drive faster than is safe for conditions.

days.title: Speed limits
days.work: Make a chart of limits: 65 mph max on most highways, 55 for two-lane undivided roads and when towing, 25 in residential and school zones, 15 at blind intersections and railroad crossings.

days.title: Stopping distance
days.work: Calculate reaction and braking distance at 25, 45 and 65 mph and graph how distance grows with speed.

days.title: 3-second rule
days.work: As a passenger, practice counting 3 seconds behind the vehicle ahead and note when to increase following distance.

days.title: Unit 2 test
days.work: Unit 2 test on signs, signals, right-of-way and speed.

objectives: Describe correct turning and lane-change procedures

days.title: Signaling
days.work: Learn hand and turn signals; signal at least 100 feet before turning and 5 seconds before a freeway lane change.

days.title: Right & left turns
days.work: Diagram right turns (merging into bike lane within 200 feet) and left turns from two-way and one-way streets.

days.title: U-turns
days.work: List where U-turns are legal and illegal in California.

days.title: Lane changes
days.work: Learn the signal–mirror–over-shoulder–go sequence and practice the head check as a passenger.

days.title: Check
days.work: Diagram quiz on turns and lane changes.

objectives: Explain safe passing and lane choice

days.title: Lane choice
days.work: Learn which lane to use for through traffic, passing and turning.

days.title: Passing
days.work: Learn when passing is illegal (curves, hills, intersections, solid lines) and the steps to pass safely.

days.title: Being passed
days.work: Learn what to do when another driver passes you.

days.title: Center turn lane
days.work: Learn rules for two-way center left-turn lanes (no more than 200 feet).

days.title: Check
days.work: Scenario quiz.

objectives: Explain parking rules and hill parking

days.title: Parking rules
days.work: List places you may never park (within 15 feet of a fire hydrant, in crosswalks, bike lanes, etc.).

days.title: Hill parking
days.work: Model hill parking with a toy car on a book ramp: uphill/downhill, with and without curb.

days.title: Parallel parking
days.work: Watch a demonstration and write the step-by-step parallel parking procedure.

days.title: Accessible parking
days.work: Learn disabled-parking rules and penalties.

days.title: Check
days.work: Parking quiz.

objectives: Explain merging, exiting and HOV lanes

days.title: Entering
days.work: Learn to use the on-ramp acceleration lane to match speed and merge into a gap.

days.title: Freeway travel
days.work: Learn lane choice, following distance and scanning on freeways.

days.title: Exiting
days.work: Learn to plan exits early and use the deceleration lane.

days.title: HOV lanes
days.work: Learn carpool lane rules and markings.

days.title: Check
days.work: Freeway quiz with diagrams.

objectives: Describe how to share the road with vulnerable users and large vehicles

days.title: Pedestrians & cyclists
days.work: Learn the 3-foot passing rule for bicycles and how to share bike lanes when turning.

days.title: Motorcycles
days.work: Learn about motorcycle visibility and lane splitting in California.

days.title: Trucks & buses
days.work: Learn about truck 'no-zones' and wide turns; sit in a parked car near a truck diagram to visualize blind spots.

days.title: Light rail & slow vehicles
days.work: Learn light rail rules and slow-moving vehicle signs.

days.title: Unit 3 test
days.work: Unit 3 test on navigating roadways and sharing the road.

objectives: Adjust driving for weather and night

days.title: Night driving
days.work: Learn headlight rules (30 min after sunset; when wipers are on) and high-beam use.

days.title: Rain & fog
days.work: Learn about slippery first rain, hydroplaning and fog driving with low beams.

days.title: Skids
days.work: Learn skid recovery: ease off pedals and steer where you want to go.

days.title: Wildfire smoke & wind
days.work: Learn California-specific hazards: wildfire smoke, high winds and mountain driving.

days.title: Check
days.work: Hazard scenario quiz.

weeks.topic: Defensive driving and the Move Over law
objectives: Apply scanning and space-management

days.title: Scanning
days.work: Practice looking 10–15 seconds ahead while a passenger and call out hazards.

days.title: Space cushion
days.work: Learn to keep space ahead, behind and to the sides.

days.title: Hazard perception
days.work: Watch dash-cam clips and identify hazards before they happen.

days.title: Move Over & work zones
days.work: Learn the Move Over law and double fines in work zones.

days.title: Check
days.work: Hazard perception test.

objectives: Explain effects of alcohol and drugs on driving
Know DUI laws

days.title: Effects
days.work: Learn how alcohol, cannabis and medications affect judgment, vision and reaction time.

days.title: BAC laws
days.work: Learn BAC limits (0.08 adults, 0.01 under 21) and implied consent.

days.title: Penalties
days.work: Research DUI penalties for minors in California, including license suspension.

days.title: Decision-making
days.work: Role-play refusing a ride with an impaired driver.

days.title: Check
days.work: DUI law quiz.

objectives: Explain distraction types and phone laws

days.title: Types
days.work: Learn visual, manual and cognitive distraction.

days.title: Phone laws
days.work: Learn California phone laws (minors may not use any device, even hands-free).

days.title: Reaction test
days.work: Test reaction time with and without texting on an online reaction test.

days.title: Drowsy driving
days.work: Learn signs of drowsiness and prevention.

days.title: Unit 4 test
days.work: Unit 4 test.

objectives: Explain what to do after a collision
Know financial responsibility

days.title: After a collision
days.work: Learn steps: stop, help injured, call 911, exchange information, report SR-1 within 10 days if required.

days.title: Insurance
days.work: Learn minimum insurance and financial responsibility.

days.title: Point count
days.work: Learn the negligent operator point system and teen penalties.

days.title: Emergencies
days.work: Learn what to do for brake failure, tire blowout and stalled on railroad tracks.

days.title: Check
days.work: Quiz.

weeks.topic: Permit test preparation and semester final
objectives: Pass full-length practice knowledge tests

days.title: Practice test 1
days.work: Take a full-length DMV-style practice test and review missed questions.

days.title: Targeted review
days.work: Review handbook sections for missed questions.

days.title: Practice test 2
days.work: Take a second practice test aiming for 90%.

days.title: Semester final
days.work: Take the semester final exam.

days.title: Next steps
days.work: Complete a checklist for applying for a permit (DL 44 form online, documents, appointment).

objectives: Apply check-call-care

days.title: Check-Call-Care
days.work: Learn the emergency action steps and practice scene-safety checks.

days.title: Calling 911
days.work: Practice what to tell a 911 dispatcher.

days.title: Good Samaritan
days.work: Learn California's Good Samaritan protections and consent.

days.title: First aid kit
days.work: Build or inventory a home and car first aid kit.

days.title: Check
days.work: Quiz.

objectives: Perform adult CPR and use an AED

days.title: Chain of survival
days.work: Learn the chain of survival.

days.title: Compressions
days.work: Practice compressions at 100–120 per minute to 'Stayin' Alive' on a pillow or manikin.

days.title: Breaths
days.work: Practice rescue breaths on a manikin.

days.title: AED
days.work: Learn AED steps with a trainer video.

days.title: Skills check
days.work: Demonstrate CPR for 2 minutes.

objectives: Perform choking relief
Adapt CPR for children and infants

days.title: Adult choking
days.work: Practice abdominal thrusts on a pillow-wrapped chair back and back blows, then self-rescue thrusts against a chair.

days.title: Child CPR
days.work: Learn child CPR differences (one or two hands, about 2 inches deep) and practice 5 cycles of 30:2 on a manikin or pillow.

days.title: Infant CPR
days.work: Practice infant CPR on a doll using two fingers or two thumbs, about 1.5 inches deep, at 100–120 per minute.

days.title: Infant choking
days.work: Practice infant choking relief with 5 back blows and 5 chest thrusts on a doll, supporting the head.

days.title: Skills check
days.work: Demonstrate adult, child and infant choking relief and child/infant CPR for a parent using a skills checklist.

weeks.assessment: Choking and pediatric CPR skills checklist.

objectives: Treat bleeding, burns, fractures and sudden illness

days.title: Bleeding control
days.work: Practice direct pressure, wound packing on a rolled towel, and applying a commercial or improvised tourniquet 2–3 inches above a wound (Stop the Bleed method).

days.title: Burns
days.work: Learn first aid for thermal, chemical and electrical burns: cool with running water 10+ minutes, cover loosely, and know when to call 911.

days.title: Fractures & sprains
days.work: Splint a 'forearm fracture' with a rolled magazine and triangular bandage and practice RICE for sprains.

days.title: Sudden illness
days.work: Learn signs and responses for stroke (BE-FAST), heart attack, seizures, diabetic emergencies and anaphylaxis using an epinephrine auto-injector trainer video.

days.title: Scenario quiz
days.work: Respond to 10 written emergency scenarios, listing the correct first aid steps for each.

objectives: Respond to heat, cold and water emergencies

days.title: Heat & cold
days.work: Compare heat exhaustion vs. heat stroke and frostbite vs. hypothermia; make a quick-reference card for hiking and sports.

days.title: Water safety
days.work: Learn drowning signs (quiet, vertical, no waving) and reach-throw-don't-go rescue; practice a throw with a rope and floating bottle.

days.title: Mock emergencies
days.work: Run three mock scenarios with family (unresponsive adult, bleeding cyclist, choking child), rotating rescuer and patient roles.

days.title: Certification
days.work: Complete an online/blended Red Cross or AHA First Aid/CPR/AED course module or schedule an in-person skills session.

days.title: Unit test
days.work: Unit 6 test: written exam plus timed CPR/AED skills demonstration.

objectives: Describe common conditions and treatments

days.title: Mental health continuum
days.work: Learn the mental health continuum (thriving to struggling) and place everyday examples on it.

days.title: Conditions
days.work: Research anxiety disorders and depression on KidsHealth and list symptoms, causes and treatments (therapy, medication, lifestyle).

days.title: Brain & body
days.work: Explain how sleep, exercise and social connection affect mood, using evidence from a reliable article.

days.title: Stigma
days.work: Analyze how media portray mental illness in two examples and rewrite one stigmatizing message.

days.title: Quiz
days.work: Quiz on common conditions and treatments.

objectives: Practice stress management

days.title: Stress log
days.work: Track stressors and physical stress responses for three days and identify patterns.

days.title: Coping strategies
days.work: Practice box breathing, progressive muscle relaxation and a 10-minute mindfulness exercise; rate which helped most.

days.title: I-statements
days.work: Practice assertive communication by rewriting five blaming statements as I-statements and role-playing two.

days.title: Conflict resolution
days.work: Use a five-step conflict-resolution model to role-play a disagreement with a sibling or friend.

days.title: Wellness plan
days.work: Write a personal wellness plan with three coping strategies, two trusted adults and daily habits.

objectives: Recognize warning signs and get help

days.title: Warning signs
days.work: Learn suicide warning signs and risk and protective factors from a reliable source.

days.title: Ask, care, tell
days.work: Practice asking directly and caringly ('Are you thinking about suicide?') and listening without judgment through scripted role-plays.

days.title: 988 and resources
days.work: Learn how the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline works (call, text, chat) and list school, county and online resources.

days.title: Safety plan
days.work: Complete a sample safety plan template and identify who you would tell if a friend were at risk.

days.title: Unit test
days.work: Unit 7 test on mental health, coping and suicide prevention.

objectives: Explain effects

days.title: Alcohol
days.work: Learn how alcohol affects the brain and body, BAC factors, and signs of alcohol poisoning (call 911).

days.title: Nicotine & vaping
days.work: Read NIDA information on nicotine addiction and vaping ingredients; analyze a vape ad for targeting of teens.

days.title: Teen brain
days.work: Explain why the developing adolescent brain is more vulnerable to addiction.

days.title: Influences
days.work: List peer, family, media and advertising influences on substance use and rate their strength.

days.title: Quiz
days.work: Quiz on alcohol and nicotine effects.

objectives: Explain risks

days.title: Cannabis
days.work: Learn short- and long-term effects of cannabis, including on memory, mental health and driving.

days.title: Prescription misuse
days.work: Learn risks of misusing prescription stimulants and opioids and how to dispose of medicines safely.

days.title: Fentanyl
days.work: Learn why counterfeit pills can contain lethal fentanyl and the signs of opioid overdose.

days.title: Naloxone
days.work: Watch a naloxone (Narcan) nasal-spray training video and practice the steps; learn California pharmacies provide it without a prescription.

days.title: Quiz
days.work: Quiz on cannabis, opioids and overdose response.

objectives: Demonstrate refusal skills
Advocate for substance-free choices

days.title: Refusal skills
days.work: Learn refusal strategies (say no firmly, give a reason, suggest an alternative, leave) and practice five scenarios.

days.title: Media literacy
days.work: Analyze an alcohol or cannabis ad for target audience and persuasive techniques.

days.title: Getting help
days.work: Locate local treatment and prevention services and a confidential youth helpline.

days.title: Advocacy
days.work: Create a poster or 60-second video encouraging peers to stay substance-free with accurate facts.

days.title: Unit test
days.work: Unit 8 test on substance use prevention.

objectives: Interpret food labels
Plan balanced meals for an active teen

days.title: Food labels
days.work: Read three food labels and compare serving size, added sugars, sodium and fiber.

days.title: Food log
days.work: Log meals for three days and compare to MyPlate recommendations for an active teen.

days.title: Fueling performance
days.work: Plan pre- and post-activity snacks and hydration for a sports day.

days.title: Disordered eating
days.work: Learn warning signs of eating disorders and where to get help.

days.title: Meal plan
days.work: Create a one-day balanced meal plan within a budget and cook one meal.

weeks.topic: Consumer health and health care access
objectives: Evaluate health products and claims
Explain how to access health services

days.title: Advertising claims
days.work: Analyze five supplement or skin-care ads for health claims and evidence.

days.title: Reliable information
days.work: Evaluate three health websites using the CRAAP test.

days.title: Health care access
days.work: Learn how to make an appointment, use insurance cards, and what confidential services minors can access in California.

days.title: Product comparison
days.work: Compare cost per use of two health products (sunscreen, toothpaste) and their active ingredients.

days.title: Consumer project
days.work: Write a consumer guide on choosing a safe product or app.

objectives: Explain how air, water and heat affect health

days.title: Air quality
days.work: Check AirNow AQI for your city and learn health actions for each AQI level, especially during wildfire smoke.

days.title: Water
days.work: Read your local water quality report and explain one contaminant tested.

days.title: Heat & climate
days.work: Learn about extreme heat health risks and community cooling centers.

days.title: Home safety
days.work: Do a home environmental health audit (smoke/CO detectors, mold, chemicals storage).

days.title: Unit test
days.work: Unit 9 test on nutrition, consumer and environmental health.

objectives: Describe healthy relationships
Explain affirmative consent

days.title: Healthy vs. unhealthy
days.work: Sort relationship behaviors on a continuum from healthy to abusive.

days.title: Consent
days.work: Learn affirmative consent and practice clear communication of boundaries in scenarios.

days.title: Digital relationships
days.work: Discuss online safety, sexting laws and digital dating abuse.

days.title: Getting help
days.work: Learn signs of dating violence and resources such as Love Is Respect.

days.title: Quiz
days.work: Quiz on healthy relationships and consent.

objectives: Explain how to access accurate information and confidential services

days.title: Accurate information
days.work: Review medically accurate information on preventing pregnancy and STIs as required by the CA Healthy Youth Act.

days.title: Services
days.work: Locate confidential sexual and reproductive health services for teens in your county.

days.title: Decision-making
days.work: Apply a decision-making model to a relationship scenario.

days.title: Communication
days.work: Practice talking with a parent or trusted adult about health questions.

days.title: Quiz
days.work: Quiz on sexual health and services.

objectives: Review driver education, first aid and Health II content

days.title: Driver ed review
days.work: Review Semester 1 driver education with a practice DMV knowledge test.

days.title: First aid review
days.work: Review first aid and CPR with scenario cards and a 2-minute CPR practice.

days.title: Health II review
days.work: Review mental health, substances, nutrition and relationships with flashcards.

days.title: Practice exam
days.work: Take a practice final exam.

days.title: Targeted study
days.work: Study weak areas from the practice exam.

weeks.topic: Final exam and personal health plan
objectives: Demonstrate mastery of course knowledge and skills

days.title: Final exam
days.work: Take the written final exam.

days.title: Skills final
days.work: Demonstrate CPR/AED and one first aid skill.

days.title: Personal health plan
days.work: Write a personal health plan with goals in three areas.

days.title: Permit check
days.work: Confirm next steps toward the learner's permit.

days.title: Reflection
days.work: Reflect on how the course will change your choices.
